findings.finding: The unit scope names "catalog completion (test, smoke, changelog asks)". The test phase adds only `out-of-sequence-continue`, `dev-server-port`, and `fix-attempts-exhausted`; the changelog phase adds three. If the test-phase skill has other interactive asks (e.g. flaky-E2E retry confirmation, blocked manual-step confirmation per migration-safety "wait for user confirmation"), they remain uncataloged — the docs edited in this diff (`migration-safety.md`, `step-3-playwright-e2e.md`) describe additional decision points not represented as gates. Verify the completion list against the test/changelog skill text; missing gates will fall through to `interactive` in a driven run and stall an unattended run.
findings.suggestion: Cross-check every AskUserQuestion site in the test/changelog skills against the catalog; add any missing gate ids or record them explicitly as `pending_phases`.

findings.finding: The AC requires "every D6 consumer of the autonomy value (produce the grep list in the PR)". The diff updates many prose consumers, but this cannot be verified from the diff alone; any consumer that branches on `autonomy == "autonomous"` in code (not markdown) would still miss `unattended`. The two code touchpoints shown are `cli.py` and the resolver; if other Python scripts compare autonomy strings, they are unhandled here.
findings.suggestion: Grep for `autonomous` across `/scripts/` and include the list in the PR; patch any code-level equality checks.

findings.finding: The schema test asserts `{"guided","autonomous","unattended","supervised"} <= set(enum)` but never pins that `unattended` is accepted end-to-end by anything other than the CLI choices — it passes even if downstream write-config validation (schema validation in `orchestrator_pkg`) rejects `unattended`. It's a weak test if write-config validates against the schema; the parametrized CLI test does cover the write path, so risk is low, but the schema assertion on `supervised` is unrelated scope creep that could mask a deliberate narrowing later.
findings.suggestion: Fine as-is, but consider asserting the enum exactly if the set is meant to be closed.

findings.finding: autonomy ""` (explicit empty string) silently falls back to the run-config value via `args.autonomy or read_run_config_autonomy(...)`. A caller explicitly passing an empty autonomy to force "no autonomy" gets the config's `unattended` instead. Minor, but it's the same class of precedence bug `--mode` solves with an explicit sentinel.
findings.suggestion: Use `args.autonomy if args.autonomy is not None else read_run_config_autonomy(...)`.  Checked and found sound: `unattended_answer_for` fails closed on unvalidated/ineligible gates (verified by the mutating test); `resolve_gate_policy` returns `unattended_answer: None` in inert mode; `should_stop` is never changed by autonomy; `validate_unattended`'s ordering and type checks; the denylist pinning tests would genuinely catch edits; `read_run_config_autonomy` mirrors the total-read guard of `read_run_config_mode`.  Overall assessment: The core mechanism (allowlist, validator, denylist, resolver plumbing, tests) is solid and well-tested; the gaps are the likely-stale generated `gate_catalog.md` and unverified completeness of the gate/consumer inventories — ship-with-fixes after regenerating the doc and confirming the grep list.
